quotes.quote: Our best result (accuracy: 91.38%) for this dataset with the fisheye-transformation appears with a window size of 543 pixels with a focal length of 130 arbitrary units when we used ResNet50.
Deep learning calculations were run 5–5 times on both the baseline and the fisheye transformed data. At the 0.05 level, the 7.07% difference in accuracy is significant.

quotes.quote: For image classification we used Matlab R2019b and its Deep Learning Toolbox (version 13.0). This toolbox provides a framework to design or implement networks, pre-trained models, and apps. Two networks pre-trained on ImageNet, ResNet50 and InceptionV3 were utilised for transfer learning.
The deep-learning parameters used: MiniBatchSize: 64, MaxEpochs: 100, InitialLearnRate: 3e-4, LearnRateDropFactor: 0.3, LearnRateDropPeriod: 50, Shuffle: every epoch.

specification.exact_target: Best classification accuracy for the MCF-7 cell culture dataset using fisheye transformation with ResNet50, window size 543 pixels, focal length 130 arbitrary units: 91.38%.
specification.blind_target: The best classification accuracy achieved on the MCF-7 cell culture dataset when using the fisheye transformation with the ResNet50 model, at the optimal window size and focal length.
specification.target_location: Results section, subsection 'Increased classification accuracy on images of cell cultures' and STAR Methods 'Quantification and statistical analysis' subsection 'MCF-7'.

location_quotes.quote: The best performance was achieved when we applied a window size of 543 pixels (211.91 μm) with a focal length of 130 arbitrary units (where 1 unit corresponds to the size of a pixel), using the ResNet50 model. In this case, accuracy reached 91.38%, which is 7% better than that achieved when using deep learning only (84.31%).
Our best result (accuracy: 91.38%) for this dataset with the fisheye-transformation appears with a window size of 543 pixels with a focal length of 130 arbitrary units when we used ResNet50.

method_quotes.quote: For image classification we used Matlab R2019b and its Deep Learning Toolbox (version 13.0). This toolbox provides a framework to design or implement networks, pre-trained models, and apps. Two networks pre-trained on ImageNet, ResNet50 and InceptionV3 were utilised for transfer learning.
The deep-learning parameters used: MiniBatchSize: 64, MaxEpochs: 100, InitialLearnRate: 3e-4, LearnRateDropFactor: 0.3, LearnRateDropPeriod: 50, Shuffle: every epoch.
Three independent trials were run for each dataset.
We applied the following standard geometry transformations on our training datasets: reflection in the left-right and a top-bottom directions, rotation, horizontal and vertical scaling.

specification.input_notes: The MCF-7 dataset is from the Broad Bioimage Benchmark Collection (BBBC021) and is not included in the deposit listing. The listed files are for UBC, LC, and iWildCam datasets. The MCF-7 images and annotations are external and must be obtained separately.

specification.comparison_metric: The observed accuracy from re-running the method is compared to the reported accuracy of 91.38%.
specification.numerical_agreement_criterion: Performance metrics on the identical split: the re-run accuracy should match the reported value within the displayed rounding bin (i.e., 91.38% to two decimal places).
specification.specification_gaps: The exact train/validation split for the MCF-7 dataset is not specified in the paper; the random seed for data augmentation and training is not given; the exact preprocessing steps for the MCF-7 images (e.g., cropping, resizing) are described but not fully detailed; the number of training epochs and early stopping criteria are not specified.
